items.title: Is the AI Bubble Popping?
items.description:
Recorded November 5, 2026.

Last Thursday, Alphabet, Google's parent company, lost nearly $500 billion in a single day, its worst day since it went public in 2004. A week later, on November 5, AI stocks fell together and the Nasdaq slid into a correction. So is the AI bubble popping?

In this episode I measure the sell-off against the line one big study uses for a crash, look at what Big Tech is spending on AI and what companies say they're getting back, compare it with the dot-com crash, and hold chip stocks up to the warning signs that came before past crashes. Then I tell you what I think it means for your retirement account and your career.

So what do you think? Is the AI bubble popping, or is this just a bad few weeks? Leave me your thoughts in the comments.

Chapters
0:00 Two big drops
0:54 What a pop looks like
1:29 How far we've fallen
2:06 Why investors are spooked
3:45 The last time a bubble popped
4:36 Will it keep going?
5:39 What it means for you
6:20 My answer

More from me: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC-N6X4gJtGrTDSAuOea8nEA · Instagram https://www.instagram.com/davidpark_phd/

items.title: Should We Shut Down Business Schools?
items.description:
Should we shut down business schools? Christopher Marquis, a professor who has taught at Harvard Business School, Cornell and Cambridge, argued in The New York Times that we should. I teach at a business school myself, so I've got skin in this game.

In this episode I lay out his case: students who arrive wanting to bring clean energy to market and leave chasing consulting and finance jobs, Harvard cases that praised Enron, and a study that found pay fell at companies that switched to a CEO with a business degree. Then I give you my three reasons for disagreeing, and where I think he's right.

So what do you think? Should we shut down business schools, or fix them? Tell me in the comments.
